title: Adaptive exposure safeguard heuristics (working)
content:
Context and intent:

This is a working scratchpad for an adaptive exposure model used when we need to gradually increase traffic to a change (model variant, routing policy, batching config) while letting runtime signals automatically gate and slow or reverse exposure. Goal: reduce manual intervention and make small-batch releases resilient to transient noise and correlated failure modes.

Scope:
- Applies to feature rollouts that affect inference execution or output distribution (model weight swaps, quantization profile changes, new reranker, alternative routing).
- Not intended for large schema changes or migrations that require database changes.
- Primary consumers: Release engineers, product rollout stewards, SRE on-call.

Definitions (short):
- Exposure unit: smallest allocatable traffic cohort (e.g., 0.1% of requests).
- Hold window: observation window after a ramp action (default 10 minutes for perf signals, 1 hour for quality signals).
- Commitment signal: telemetry we treat as high-confidence and low-noise (p95 latency, 5xx ratio, request drop rate).
- Quality probe: synthetic prompt set run against live variant and baseline periodically to estimate semantic/regression signals.

Adaptive exposure algorithm (overview):
1) Start at baseline allocation A0 (usually 0%).
2) Ramp plan: predefined steps by exposure unit [0.1%, 0.5%, 1%, 2%, 5%, 10%] with time-based minimums (t_min_per_step).
3) After each step, wait hold window then evaluate commit signals. If all pass, advance to next step. If any fail, take mitigation (backoff or revert).
4) If noise is detected (flapping metrics), automatically extend hold window once then proceed if stable.
5) If quality probe degrades beyond threshold, immediately revert to last known-good allocation and create incident if degradation is sustained for >3 consecutive probes.

Heuristics and concrete thresholds (starting point — to iterate):
- Latency: p95 increase > 30% relative to baseline over hold window -> throttle (reduce by 50% of current step). p95 increase > 60% -> immediate revert to previous stable allocation.
- Error budget: if 5xx rate > 0.5% absolute or increases by 3x baseline -> throttle. If sustained > 1% for > 5m -> revert.
- Cost spike: token-cost/spend rate increases > 40% -> alert + pause further ramps. If paired with latency/quality regressions, revert.
- Quality probe: semantic-F1 (or chosen metric) drop > 5 absolute points -> revert. Drop between 2–5 -> pause and run extended probe set.
- User-facing regression (explicit bug reports or SLA violations): immediate rollback regardless of other signals.

Traffic allocation schedule examples:
- Conservative path: 0.1% -> wait 30m -> 0.5% -> wait 60m -> 1% -> wait 2h -> 2% -> wait 4h -> 5%
- Fast path (low-risk config-only): 0.5% -> wait 15m -> 2% -> wait 30m -> 10%
Choice depends on change type (model swap vs. config tweak).

Gating policy matrix (example mapping):
- Change type = model-binary-swap (non-breaking): require quality probe + commit signals. Default: conservative path.
- Change type = latency-optimization (kernel change/quantization): require latency + error/gap checks, fast path allowed.
- Change type = routing-policy: require traffic continuity checks and per-region verification.

Mitigation actions (ordered):
1) Pause further ramps and extend hold window by factor 2.
2) Reduce allocation to last stable step and notify stakeholders.
3) If health does not recover within extended hold window: revert to pre-change allocation and trigger postmortem cadence.
4) In urgent cases (customer outage, SLA breach): immediate rollback and page on-call SRE.

Instrumentation checklist (must be present before using adaptive exposure):
- Per-variant, per-route p50/p95/p99 latency streams (1m granularity).
- Per-variant error code breakdown (4xx/5xx and internal error buckets).
- Live quality probe runner producing hourly diffs vs baseline (storing example traces).
- Token cost / egress cost per variant per minute.
- Canary cohort-level user impact sampling (capture anonymized snippets for inspection).
- Synthetic traffic generator to reproduce observed failures.

Dashboards and alerts (templates to standardize):
- "Adaptive-exposure / [change-id] / health" dashboard with commit signal strip for last 24h.
- Alert: adaptive-exposure/commit-failure (firing when combined health score < threshold for 5m).
- Alert: quality-probe/regression (firing when probe metric crosses threshold twice in a row).

Quality probe details (practical notes):
- Start with 100 high-signal prompts representative of critical workloads. Run probe every 15m against baseline and variant with recorded metrics (F1, BLEU when applicable, reranker score stability).
- Keep golden examples in artifact storage for reproducibility. Include a small reranking human review queue for severe regressions.

Simulation plan (to validate heuristics):
- Run traffic replay with injected latency spikes (10%, 30%, 60% p95 increases) and assert adaptive exposure reduces allocation per heuristic.
- Simulate quality drift by transforming probe outputs (introduce synonym swaps, hallucinations) and assert probe triggers revert when thresholds crossed.
- Validate false-positive rate by running 48h of noise-only traffic and ensuring algorithm does not revert more than 1% of the time.

Operational playbook snippets (to paste into runbooks):
- If alert adaptive-exposure/commit-failure fires: 1) Owner page SRE rotation + release steward. 2) Immediately pause any scheduled ramp in console. 3) Check quality probe diffs and top-10 slow traces. 4) If revert happened automatically, confirm revert was to correct model id and annotate rollout.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- How do we combine noisy telemetry signals into a single "health score"? Candidate: weighted z-scores across latency, error, and probe metrics. Wondering if a simple rule-based system is safer initially.
- What is the minimum viable probe set size/time to detect semantic regressions reliably? 100 prompts? 250? Tradeoff: probe runtime cost vs sensitivity.
- Should we allow conditional fast-paths for specific low-risk teams? (e.g., internal-only releases)

Immediate next steps (actionable):
- (ENG-7891) Implement per-variant cost and latency streams by 2025-01-24 (owner: Marcus).
- Build a lightweight health-score prototype that combines p95 and 5xx (PR: platform/pull/1428). Target: 2025-02-06.
- Draft a short operator-facing runbook (this doc -> runbook) and coordinate with SRE team for on-call paging thresholds (Priya).

Notes to self / scratch items:
- Keep algorithm auditable: every automated action must write an immutable event with reason, metrics snapshot, and executed-by=adaptive-exposure-service.
- Consider usage of model-similarity-based checks (embedding distance of outputs to baseline) as a secondary quality probe.
- Log sample user requests that triggered decisions (redact PII) for postmortem analysis.

This is intentionally iterative. The thresholds above are starting points for lab testing and should be tuned based on replay experiments and a couple of low-risk live rollouts. If anyone reading wants to propose alternate thresholds, leave comments or reference ENG-7891 and ping on slack:#rollouts-thread-923.
